pr.title: Merge stores entry by entry, and keep each entry's earlier secrets
pr.head: f7a68da5c38893b823c0496f95e496ebb74ad951

summary: multipass keeps every password in one text document, encrypted as one age file. Each save replaces the whole file, so when two Macs each change a copy, nothing can combine them and one copy's changes are lost. The next plan in line, vault-key, writes every save as a new file and needs a way to combine the files it finds into one store. This pull request supplies that combination.
It does so with a new store text, format 3, and a merge function:

1. Every entry records when it last changed. A modified line holds the time in milliseconds. A change is stamped one millisecond past the newest stamp in the store it was made from, so a change made after seeing another always wins, even when clocks disagree.
  2. Removing an entry leaves a tombstone. rm keeps the name with modified and deleted, so a merge can tell a removal from an entry it has never seen.
  3. Stores merge entry by entry. Store::merge keeps each name's newest version, so every Mac that merges the same files writes the same store. Nothing outside the tests calls it yet; vault-key is its first caller.
  4. Each entry keeps its earlier secrets. previous-secret and previous-otp lines hold replaced secrets and setup keys. A merge turns the losing version's secret into history, so a merge never drops a secret. multipass history lists the dates, and multipass get --previous <n> prints one.

multipass still reads formats 1 and 2, whose entries read as modified 0, and writes format 3. An older multipass refuses a format 3 store with the store uses format 3, but this multipass reads formats 1 and 2.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Stamp: an entry's modified value, milliseconds since 1970.
  • Version: one name's state in one store, a live entry or a tombstone, with its stamp and history.
  • Tombstone: a removed entry, kept as its name, modified, deleted, and history lines.
  • History: an entry's earlier secrets and setup keys, each with the time it was replaced.
  • Cutoffs: the three times before which to_text leaves things out when it writes the store.

cards.title: What is kept, and for how long
cards.html:
WhatKept
A live entry's earlier secrets and setup keysThe newest 10 of each, or every one replaced in the past year, whichever is more
A removed entry's secrets and setup key30 days
A removed entry's marker120 days
A removed entry's username and notesNot kept

Each limit applies when multipass writes the store, not when a read opens it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review of this head asked for two changes, both to the README's account of rm: a removed secret can outlive the 30 days the README promises, and undoing a removal brings back only the secret.
  • The code, the format, and the merge laws matched the plan, and fmt, clippy, tests, the dependency check, and CI passed.
  • Stock age was not installed where the review ran, so no store from this head was decrypted with age -d in the review.

groups.title: Format 3, history, and the merge
groups.kicker: The store module: the new text, the version type, and how two stores combine.
intro: All of the change's logic lives in src/store.rs. The store maps each name to a Version: a live entry or a tombstone, its stamp, and its History. Every change goes through insert or remove, which take a stamp and move the replaced secret and setup key into the history. The old get_mut, which changed an entry without a stamp, is gone.

Version::join is the merge of two versions of one name. It keeps the one with the newer stamp, breaks a tie by comparing the versions' text without their history, and takes the union of both histories plus each version's own secret and setup key. A losing value is dated by its own version's stamp, not the winner's, which is what keeps the merge commutative, associative, and idempotent: two Macs that merge the same files in any order write the same store.
Nothing is pruned in the merge. to_text applies the three cutoffs when it writes the store, so pruning depends on when the store is written, and the merge stays a pure union.

checks.text: The plan's § 2.1 table is the format's definition. A field line always starts with a tab, and names escape tab, newline, carriage return, and backslash, so an entry name can never read as a modified, deleted, or previous-* line.

files.note: The format 3 text, Version and History, stamps, Store::merge, the cutoffs, and the reader for formats 1 to 3.

checks.text: The merge laws hold with history included. The review walked join and normalize by hand, and merge_is_commutative_associative_and_idempotent passed over 3,000 generated triples.

put carries a tombstone's history into an entry added again under the same name. When no save has run since 30 days after the removal, the removed secret becomes the new entry's history and is kept for a year. A temporary test reproduced it at this head; the review's README thread covers it.
The cutoffs apply only here, when the store is written. A store that is only read keeps whatever it held at its last save.
Malformed lines fail with only their line number. rejects_malformed_text covers a missing or misplaced modified, a tombstone with a field, and history dated after the entry or with no value.

groups.title: The CLI: stamps, history, and --previous
groups.kicker: How each command stamps its change, and the two new ways to read history.
intro: run reads the clock once, and each saving command (add, rm, otp --set, otp --clear) takes a stamp from the store it opened, warns when that stamp is more than a day ahead of the clock, and saves with Cutoffs::at(now).

Two read commands are new. multipass history <name> lists when the entry changed and when each earlier value was replaced, and never shows a value. multipass get <name> --previous <n> prints or copies the nth most recently replaced secret, or with --field otp the setup key. Both also find a removed entry. Without --previous, get still prints the current value.

files.note: Stamps for each saving command, the history command, get --previous, and a UTC date formatter.

checks.text: Errors from previous_value name only a count, such as x has only 2 earlier secrets. The review saw this against a release build driven with expect, and previous_counts_from_the_most_recently_replaced covers it.
history prints dates and no value. history_lists_dates_and_no_values checks that no secret or key appears, and the release build printed only dates.

groups.title: README, AGENTS.md, and the plans
groups.kicker: What users and agents are told about format 3 and history.
intro: The README gains a section on getting an earlier password back, and its recovery example shows format 3. AGENTS.md says multipass writes format 3 and that the merge must keep its laws with history included. The store-merge plan records the history design and the 30-day decision, and is marked completed with an outcome. The passkeys plan no longer calls history undecided.

files.note: A new section on earlier passwords, and the recovery example in format 3.

checks.text: The undo command brings back only the secret. rm keeps no username or notes, and the setup key needs its own restore. The README should say what rm keeps and show the setup-key restore.

"After 30 days the removed secrets are gone for good" is not what the code does. A removed secret leaves the file only at the first save 30 or more days after rm, and adding the name again before then keeps it as the new entry's history for a year.

files.note: Says multipass writes format 3, and that Store::merge must stay commutative, associative, and idempotent.
Adds § 2.6, password history, and marks the plan completed with an outcome.
Says the history in § 2.6 keeps a losing password edit, but no passkey.
